findings.evidence: The definition at lines 185–200 constructs the inverse indirectly via `Equiv.ofBijective`; the sole API lemma at lines 204–207 describes only forward application to `Quotient.mk`.
findings.fix: Add a simp/iff lemma characterizing the inverse, e.g. that its inverse equals `Quotient.mk _ x` iff the factor's underlying polynomial is `minpoly F x` (with the orientation chosen for stable simplification).
findings.issue: `orbitQuotientEquivFactors` has only the forward `mk` equation; there is no public characterization of `orbitQuotientEquivFactors ... .symm q`, leaving half of the equivalence unusable without unfolding.

summary: The orbit-factor equivalence lacks an elimination rule for its opaque, noncomputable inverse, so consumers cannot identify the orbit corresponding to a factor without reconstructing the implementation proof.
